job.system:
You are the AI assistant for the Machine Intelligence Research Institute. Our staff use you for day-to-day work: research, writing, data, scheduling, and operations.

About us: The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI) is a nonprofit based in Berkeley, California. Founded in 2000, MIRI spent two decades on technical AI alignment research; since 2023 our focus has been communications and policy. We believe that if anyone builds artificial superintelligence with anything like current techniques and understanding, the result will be human extinction. Our goal is an international prohibition on the development of superintelligence, beginning with national legislation in the United States. We work through public communication, policy advocacy, and briefing lawmakers and their staff.

Current focus: Our top priority this fall is S. 2817, the Superintelligence Prohibition Act, which we strongly support. The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up the bill on Thursday, October 15.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so work everything out directly in your reply. Staff rely on your work, so be accurate and thorough.

House side: Cannon ↔ Longworth 5 min, Longworth ↔ Rayburn 5 min, Cannon ↔ Rayburn 10 min. Any Senate building ↔ any House building: 25 min. Same building: no travel time. A team needs at least the walking time between the end of one meeting and the start of the next.

- One meeting per office is plenty.

I checked every meeting against its office's window, each team's availability, the walking times and the lunch rule. One assumption: walking time can fall inside the lunch break. For example, Team A Wednesday has 45 free minutes between Stein and Fischer, and 25 of them are the walk.

## Why some offices didn't fit

- **Okafor and Fischer can't both meet on Wednesday.** On Wednesday, Okafor (13:00–13:30), Fischer (13:00–13:15) and Doyle (13:45 only) each need a different team, and you have only two. One of Okafor or Fischer therefore has to be on Tuesday morning. Only Team A is available then, and Rourke (Tue only) has to be at 9:30. That is why Okafor is Tuesday and Fischer is Wednesday.
- **Nakamura (T2, Tue 10:45, Rayburn)** would push both Okafor and Fischer to Wednesday. Per the point above, that loses a Tier 1 meeting.
- **Brooks (T2) and Pruitt (T2)** compete for Team A's single slot after 15:00 on Wednesday, so only one fits. They are worth the same points. You could swap Pruitt for Brooks at 15:15 if you'd rather have another Senate meeting before the markup. For that version, Team A would do Doyle 13:45, Crowe 14:15 and Brooks 15:15, and Team B would do Fischer 13:00 and Abernathy 13:45.
- **Tier 3 offices left out:** Haddad, Osei, Vasquez, Kowalski, Hughes, Park, Pike, Varga and Iqbal. Each one would bump a higher-value meeting or break a walking-time or lunch constraint.

I couldn't find a schedule that scores higher than 79. A few equal-scoring variants exist, such as Park instead of Ellis, Hughes instead of Kessler, or Brooks instead of Pruitt.
